paragraphs: This paper builds a benchmark for detecting abusive language in Tigrinya social media, where limited annotated data makes content moderation research difficult. It contains 13,717 YouTube comments labeled by nine native speakers for abusiveness, sentiment, and topic. These linked annotations allow researchers to study several aspects of the same comments rather than treating abusive language as an isolated classification task.

The authors use an iterative term clustering method to select data. They also include both native Ge'ez script and Romanized Tigrinya, reflecting their finding that around 64% of Tigrinya social media content uses Romanized transliterations. Covering both writing systems matters because a benchmark restricted to the native script would miss a substantial part of actual usage.

In the reported experiments, small fine-tuned models outperform prompted frontier language models across all three tasks. For abusiveness detection, they reach 86.67% F1, more than seven points above the best evaluated LLM. The public benchmark therefore supplies both a research resource and evidence that task-specific training can be especially valuable in this low-resource setting.
neurips-2025-a-multi-task-benchmark-for-.tldr: A Tigrinya moderation benchmark covering two writing systems shows small fine-tuned models outperforming prompted frontier LLMs across three tasks.

paragraphs: This paper challenges a standard way of analyzing game-solving algorithms: generating random game trees with independently sampled leaf values. The authors argue that this independence removes structural difficulty and produces misleadingly favorable conclusions. In particular, familiar results about collapsing root values and broadly optimal algorithms can reflect the artificial model rather than meaningful strengths of the algorithms.

Their replacement generates trees incrementally, using conditional distributions that preserve dependencies on ancestors. This creates synthetic games with adjustable difficulty while keeping enough mathematical structure for analysis. The authors derive recursive descriptions of average computational cost for algorithms including AlphaBeta and Scout, allowing comparisons at tree depths where Monte Carlo simulation becomes infeasible.

Under this model, the algorithms appear to approach the same asymptotic branching factor, but that similarity conceals substantial differences on deep finite trees. AlphaBeta has a significantly larger multiplicative cost than alternatives such as Scout. The finding shows why an asymptotic growth rate alone can miss practically important slowdowns, while keeping the comparison grounded in the proposed synthetic game model.
neurips-2025-alphabeta-is-not-as-good-as.tldr: A more structured synthetic game model reveals substantial AlphaBeta slowdowns that conventional independent-leaf analyses can obscure.

paragraphs: ARMesh changes the order in which an autoregressive model builds a three-dimensional mesh. Existing approaches typically generate individual faces in a fixed lexicographic order, which does not closely follow the shape's geometric organization. This paper instead generates a simple shape first and progressively adds detail, making the sequence of predictions correspond to increasing geometric resolution.

The approach starts from mesh simplification: a process that merges faces to obtain simpler shapes. The authors train a transformer to approximate the reverse of that process. They generalize meshes to simplicial complexes so generation can begin with a single point, then add geometry through local remeshing. The connections within the shape are allowed to change rather than being fixed beforehand.

Experiments show that this progressive process provides a practical control over generation time and detail: stopping earlier yields an earlier level of refinement. The same approach also supports mesh refinement and editing. Its contribution is therefore both a different generation order and a representation that accommodates changing geometry and topology throughout that order.
neurips-2025-armesh-autoregressive-mesh-.tldr: ARMesh generates meshes by reversing simplification, progressively adding detail while allowing topology changes and early stopping.

paragraphs: CorrectBench evaluates whether methods intended to help language models revise their answers actually improve reasoning performance. It covers commonsense reasoning, mathematical reasoning, and code generation, and compares intrinsic, external, and fine-tuned self-correction approaches. This shared evaluation makes it possible to examine self-correction across different tasks and strategies rather than drawing conclusions from a single method.

The results show that self-correction can improve accuracy, especially on complex reasoning tasks. Combining different strategies produces additional gains, but reduces efficiency. The authors also find limited additional improvement and high time costs when applying further self-correction methods to reasoning models, including the example identified in the abstract as DeepSeek-V3.

A comparatively simple chain-of-thought baseline remains competitive in both accuracy and efficiency. That finding makes the computational cost of revision central to interpreting the results: a method's value depends on more than whether it occasionally repairs an answer. The benchmark supports self-correction as a useful possibility while identifying the balance between reasoning gains and operating cost as an unresolved research challenge.
neurips-2025-can-llms-correct-themselves.tldr: CorrectBench finds that self-correction can improve reasoning accuracy, but added time costs can make simple chain-of-thought prompting competitive.

paragraphs: This paper studies the consistency of physics-informed neural networks when solving second-order elliptic equations with Dirichlet boundary conditions. The central concern is whether the method reliably approaches the intended solution, rather than simply being usable as a numerical procedure. The boundary conditions and equation class define the setting in which the authors develop their guarantees.

The analysis first establishes a necessary and sufficient condition for consistency of a related physics-informed kernel gradient flow algorithm. Using neural tangent kernel theory, the authors then obtain a corresponding necessary and sufficient condition for PINNs when the network is sufficiently wide. The width requirement matters because it is part of the stated bridge from the kernel analysis to neural network training.

Under stronger assumptions, the paper also provides non-asymptotic loss bounds for both methods, addressing behavior before an asymptotic limit. Finally, the theory guides construction of a pathological example in which a PINN is inconsistent. Together, these results characterize when consistency holds in the analyzed setting and demonstrate that it cannot be taken for granted.
neurips-2025-consistency-of-physics-info.tldr: The paper characterizes PINN consistency for a specified elliptic-equation setting and constructs an example where consistency fails.

paragraphs: DisasterM3 is a remote sensing vision-language dataset designed for disaster assessment and response. It contains 26,988 bi-temporal satellite images and about 123,000 instruction pairs spanning five continents. Its 36 historical events cover ten categories of natural and human-made disasters, providing varied scenes for studying how models interpret damage and support reporting.

The dataset combines multiple sensors, including synthetic aperture radar imagery for post-disaster scenes where extreme weather can hinder optical imaging. Its nine tasks range from recognizing affected objects to assessing structural damage, reasoning about object relationships, and producing long reports. This range connects visual perception with the more involved reasoning needed to describe a disaster's consequences.

Evaluation of 14 general and remote sensing vision-language models reveals difficulties associated with limited disaster-specific training material, differences between sensors, and poor sensitivity to damaged-object counts. Fine-tuning four models on DisasterM3 produces consistent improvements, alongside reported generalization across sensors and disaster types. The results position the dataset as both a diagnostic benchmark and training material for improving performance on these demanding tasks.
neurips-2025-disasterm3-a-remote-sensing.tldr: DisasterM3 benchmarks satellite-based disaster understanding across hazards, sensors, and tasks, and improves evaluated models through targeted fine-tuning.

paragraphs: DFGauss applies progressive, coarse-to-fine prediction to indoor three-dimensional occupancy modeling. Many existing methods use dense voxel grids and convolution-heavy networks, making this kind of multiscale processing computationally expensive. The paper explores a Gaussian representation as an alternative way to organize and refine information about occupied space.

The method works directly with the parameters of three-dimensional Gaussians instead of refining voxel volumes or two-dimensional projections. At each finer scale, a Gaussian is predicted using its coarser counterpart, creating an autoregressive process across levels of resolution. Hierarchical supervision guides these successive refinements, so the representation develops detail through a structured sequence rather than a single dense prediction.

An importance-guided strategy selectively carries informative Gaussians into finer scales. This allows refinement to vary spatially, directing additional detail toward selected parts of the representation. Experiments on occupancy benchmarks report competitive performance. The stated findings support Gaussian-based autoregressive refinement as a promising direction for scalable occupancy prediction, with selective refinement supplying the method's main mechanism for improving efficiency.
neurips-2025-dynamic-focused-masking-for.tldr: DFGauss predicts 3D occupancy by progressively refining selected Gaussians, achieving competitive benchmark performance with spatially adaptive detail.

paragraphs: This paper improves algorithms for two extensions of correlation clustering, a problem that groups objects using graph-based similarity relationships. Chromatic correlation clustering adds semantic categories through colored edge labels. Pseudometric-weighted correlation clustering instead allows different edge weights, subject to the triangle inequality. Both settings represent relationships richer than a simple binary similarity label.

The authors combine linear programming relaxations with pivoting and rounding rules tailored to each problem. The relaxation supplies a mathematical starting point, while rounding turns that solution into a clustering. Their guarantees measure how much worse the resulting clustering can be than an optimal one, making a smaller approximation ratio a stronger worst-case result.

For pseudometric weights, they obtain a 10/3 approximation, matching the best possible bound within the stated standard relaxation and specialized rounding framework. For the chromatic problem, they improve the ratio from 2.5 to 2.15 and establish a 2.11 lower bound within the same analytical framework. These bounds show that the chromatic result is close to that framework's limit, without claiming a universal barrier for every possible algorithm.
neurips-2025-improved-approximation-algo.tldr: New rounding methods improve approximation guarantees for two correlation-clustering variants, with tight or near-tight bounds within the analyzed frameworks.

paragraphs: KORGym is an evaluation platform that uses more than fifty games to study language-model reasoning. Its motivation is that benchmarks confined to particular domains provide an incomplete picture of general reasoning potential. Games are available in textual or visual formats, allowing the platform to examine reasoning under different ways of presenting a problem.

The platform supports interactive assessments spanning multiple turns, as well as reinforcement learning scenarios. This broadens evaluation beyond answering a single isolated question. The authors use it to test 19 language models and eight vision-language models, then examine how modality, reasoning strategies, reinforcement learning techniques, and response length relate to performance.

The experiments reveal consistent reasoning patterns among models from the same family and stronger performance from closed-source models in the reported evaluation. These findings describe patterns within the tested collection rather than establishing a universal ranking. KORGym's contribution is a varied, interactive setting for comparing reasoning behavior and investigating how evaluation conditions and model strategies affect the results.
neurips-2025-korgym-a-dynamic-game-platf.tldr: KORGym uses over fifty interactive text and visual games to compare model reasoning and study factors affecting performance.

paragraphs: KTAE addresses how reinforcement learning assigns credit within a language model's mathematical solution. Methods such as GRPO and DAPO calculate an advantage for a complete sampled response and give every token the same value. This treats all parts of the response alike, even though individual tokens can have different relationships to whether the final answer is correct.

The proposed method estimates token importance using statistical analysis of sampled responses and their correctness. It then combines these estimates with the existing response-level advantage to produce more detailed training signals. This adds token-level distinctions without introducing an additional model, making KTAE an extension to the credit assignment used by the existing algorithms.

Across five mathematical reasoning benchmarks, the authors report that GRPO and DAPO augmented with KTAE outperform their respective baselines. The trained models achieve higher accuracy with shorter responses and also surpass R1-Distill-Qwen-1.5B when using the same base model. These findings support finer-grained advantage estimation as a way to improve the effectiveness and response efficiency of the evaluated reasoning training procedures.
neurips-2025-ktae-a-model-free-algorithm.tldr: KTAE adds statistically estimated token-level credit to reasoning reinforcement learning, improving reported accuracy while shortening responses.

paragraphs: DPRNet addresses tone mapping for high-dynamic-range images, focusing on preserving texture and structure while maintaining coherent brightness and contrast. The paper identifies two connected problems in existing methods: handcrafted detail-recovery pyramids can lose fine information, and weak coordination between global tone and local contrast can produce flat-looking images or halo artifacts.

Its core is a learned differential pyramid that adapts the differences computed across image scales to the content. This generalizes traditional Laplacian and Difference-of-Gaussian pyramids, allowing detail extraction to respond to varying brightness and contrast. Separate global tone perception and local tone tuning modules work on downsampled inputs to provide efficient tone adaptation.

An iterative enhancement module then restores the full-resolution image progressively, reinforcing structure and sharpness along the way. Experiments report state-of-the-art results, including PSNR improvements of 2.39 dB on 4K HDR+ and 3.01 dB on 4K HDRI Haven, together with perceptually coherent outputs that preserve detail. The approach links learned detail representation with coordinated tone adjustment rather than treating detail recovery as a fixed final operation.
neurips-2025-learning-differential-pyram.tldr: DPRNet learns multiscale image differences and coordinates global and local tone adjustment to improve HDR tone-mapping detail and fidelity.

paragraphs: This paper improves Direct Preference Optimization by selecting its training data more carefully. DPO aligns a language model using preferences between responses, but noisy preference data can cause parameter shrinkage. The authors focus on dataset curation as a way to address that problem, extending research that has largely concentrated on changing the optimization objective.

Their selection principle maximizes margins, using the strength of preference separation to guide curation. Because different reward models can contribute noise, they also introduce Bayesian aggregation. This combines multiple external and implicit margin sources into a single preference probability, bringing several signals together before deciding which data should support training.

The experiments report consistent data efficiency across varied settings. Using only 10% of Ultrafeedback, the approach delivers 3% to 8% improvements on AlpacaEval2 across evaluated Llama, Mistral, and Qwen models. An extension to iterative DPO gains roughly 3% with 25% of the online data. These results suggest substantial redundancy in the evaluated preference datasets and show that selecting informative examples can improve alignment while reducing the amount of training data used.
neurips-2025-less-is-more-improving-llm-.tldr: Margin-based preference selection and Bayesian aggregation improve evaluated DPO models while using substantially smaller training subsets.

paragraphs: This paper introduces a version of PAC learning in which guarantees can depend on the distribution of inputs but must apply uniformly across all target concepts. Classical nonuniform PAC learning permits the opposite dependence: guarantees may vary with the target concept, but not with the input distribution. The new formulation captures the idea that some distributions are easier to learn from.

The main result characterizes achievable learning rates through three cases. Exponential rates of the form e^{-n} occur precisely for finite hypothesis classes. Rates of the form d/n are achievable when the VC-eluder dimension d is finite. When that dimension is infinite, convergence may be arbitrarily slow. Here, n represents the amount of observed training data.

These cases connect a distribution-sensitive learning guarantee to structural properties of the hypothesis class. The authors also show that every learnable class in the original concept-dependent nonuniform model admits linear rates. Together, the results clarify how changing which aspect of a learning problem the guarantee may depend on changes the possible speed of learning.
neurips-2025-marginal-nonuniform-pac-lea.tldr: A distribution-dependent variant of PAC learning admits a three-way characterization of learning rates based on hypothesis-class structure.

paragraphs: This paper investigates why label smoothing can produce undesirable feature representations despite helping reduce overconfidence and improve generalization. The identified problems are excessive confidence on misclassified examples and overly compact feature clusters. When examples within a class become too similar in feature space, the representation loses variation that distinguishes different instances of that class.

The authors decompose the label-smoothing loss into two terms. One suppresses overconfidence when a prediction is correct; the other amplifies errors when it is wrong, encouraging unjustified certainty and worsening representation collapse. Their replacement, Max Suppression, penalizes the highest-scoring logit rather than the ground-truth logit. This applies regularization to the model's leading prediction whether or not that prediction is correct.

Feature-space analyses show that MaxSup restores variation within classes while making boundaries between classes sharper. Experiments on large-scale image classification and multiple downstream tasks support it as a more robust alternative to label smoothing. The contribution ties a specific loss mechanism to the observed collapse and changes that mechanism directly.
neurips-2025-maxsup-overcoming-represent.tldr: MaxSup penalizes the top prediction score to address label smoothing's error amplification and loss of within-class feature diversity.

paragraphs: Nemotron-Flash studies how to design small language models for actual device speed. Reducing parameter count does not necessarily yield a proportional reduction in latency. The authors identify two major architectural influences: the balance between depth and width, especially for small batches, and the choice of computational operators, which affects both latency and throughput.

Their analysis finds that deep, narrow models can be more accurate at a fixed parameter budget without offering the best accuracy-latency trade-off. They investigate efficient alternatives to attention, then use evolutionary search to discover effective combinations of operators in hybrid models. A weight normalization technique complements the architecture search by enabling more effective updates and improving convergence during training.

The resulting Nemotron-Flash family improves the reported accuracy-efficiency frontier. Compared with Qwen3-1.7B and Qwen3-0.6B, the abstract reports over 5.5% higher average accuracy, latency reductions by factors of 1.3 and 1.9, and throughput increases of 18.7 and 45.6 times, respectively. These results support treating measured execution behavior as a primary design objective rather than relying on parameter count alone.
neurips-2025-nemotron-flash-towards-late.tldr: Nemotron-Flash combines device-aware architecture search and improved training to advance the reported accuracy, latency, and throughput trade-off for small language models.

paragraphs: This paper studies stochastic minimax optimization in which the objective contains multiple nested function levels. One set of variables is minimized while another is maximized. The nesting introduces a central difficulty: stochastic gradient estimates can be biased for both sets of variables, complicating convergence analysis beyond the corresponding compositional minimization problem.

The authors propose a gradient descent-ascent algorithm with smoothing under a nonconvex-PL condition. They establish convergence to an (epsilon, epsilon/sqrt(kappa))-stationary point, with improved condition-number dependence of order kappa^{3/2}. Epsilon describes the requested accuracy and kappa is the condition number. The stated dependence therefore characterizes how this part of the guarantee scales with the problem's conditioning.

Under the separate two-sided PL condition, the authors develop a stage-wise algorithm incorporating variance reduction to address biased gradients. It enables a transition from the paired stationarity guarantee to an epsilon-stationary point. Experiments support the algorithms' effectiveness. The contribution combines algorithm design with conditional convergence guarantees, distinguishing the assumptions supporting each result rather than claiming convergence for arbitrary nested minimax problems.
neurips-2025-on-the-convergence-of-stoch.tldr: Smoothing and stage-wise variance reduction yield improved conditional convergence guarantees for stochastic multilevel compositional minimax optimization.

paragraphs: Robot-R1 trains vision-language models to reason about robot control using reinforcement learning. The paper argues that supervised fine-tuning often relies on heuristically assembled reasoning datasets that are not explicitly optimized for control. It also identifies catastrophic forgetting and reduced generalization as problems that can arise with that training approach.

The framework asks a model to predict the next keypoint state needed to complete a task. Its inputs are the current scene image and environment metadata derived from expert demonstrations. During training, Robot-R1 samples responses containing reasoning and reinforces those associated with more accurate predictions. This links the learning signal to the quality of a control-related prediction rather than only to reproducing a supplied response.

In the reported experiments, Robot-R1-trained models outperform supervised fine-tuning methods on embodied reasoning tasks. The seven-billion-parameter model also surpasses GPT-4o on reasoning related to low-level action control, including spatial and movement reasoning. These findings support reinforcement learning for the evaluated prediction and reasoning tasks; the stated comparison concerns those tasks rather than a blanket ranking of overall robotic capability.
neurips-2025-robot-r1-reinforcement-lear.tldr: Robot-R1 rewards accurate next-keypoint predictions to improve embodied reasoning, outperforming evaluated supervised approaches and GPT-4o on specified control-related tasks.

paragraphs: This paper addresses identifying and segmenting the object involved in an action described by a language query in first-person video. Such footage combines rapid motion and frequent occlusion with ambiguity about the intended object. Training data can add another problem: skewed object-action pairings may encourage models to rely on associations that do not reliably identify the object.

CERES is a plug-in framework that adapts pretrained referring-video segmentation models to this setting. It applies causal intervention ideas to both language and vision. On the language side, backdoor adjustment principles target biases learned from dataset statistics. On the visual side, front-door adjustment concepts guide the integration of semantic features and geometric depth information to address visual confounding.

The two components tackle different sources of misleading evidence in the same segmentation task. Experiments report state-of-the-art performance on egocentric referring-video benchmarks. The results support the proposed combination as a way to improve robustness in the tested setting and motivate further use of causal reasoning for understanding first-person video.
neurips-2025-robust-egocentric-referring.tldr: CERES uses causal intervention principles in language and vision to improve language-guided object segmentation in first-person videos.

paragraphs: This paper studies how to locate the origin of an anomaly when only a few, or even one, observations are available after a fault. It models the fault as a change in a causal mechanism. Existing methods can struggle because they need the post-change distribution or must evaluate regression models in poorly supported regions of the data.

The authors develop methods for the case of a single root cause and a causal graph that is a polytree. When that graph is known, they provide guarantees for a traversal algorithm using only marginal anomaly scores, which measure how unusual each variable is individually. The method does not require choosing an arbitrary threshold that separates anomalous from normal scores.

When the graph is unknown, the paper gives a causal justification for prioritizing variables with the largest marginal anomaly scores. It proves that, in polytrees, smaller-score anomalies are unlikely to cause larger-score ones and bounds the likelihood of pathways that violate score monotonicity. This supports a simple heuristic under the stated assumptions without turning it into a guaranteed rule for every anomaly.
neurips-2025-root-cause-analysis-of-outl.tldr: Under single-root-cause and polytree assumptions, marginal anomaly scores support efficient root-cause analysis even with little post-fault data.

paragraphs: SCOPE reduces the number of visual tokens processed by a multimodal language model. Many tokens contain redundant information, but simply keeping those with the highest attention-based importance can leave the retained set semantically incomplete. The paper treats token selection as a joint problem of preserving salient information and covering the image's represented content.

The method defines coverage for a selected group of tokens using relationships among tokens. For every token not yet selected, it calculates how much additional coverage that token would provide. It combines this gain with the token's saliency to form a SCOPE score, then repeatedly selects the highest-scoring candidate. Selection therefore depends on what the retained set already represents, as well as each token's importance.

Experiments use LLaVA-1.5 and LLaVA-Next across multiple vision-language understanding benchmarks. The authors report consistent improvements over prior pruning approaches. The findings support considering the selected tokens collectively: a useful additional token is one that contributes important information while extending the coverage of the tokens already kept.
neurips-2025-scope-saliency-coverage-ori.tldr: SCOPE prunes visual tokens by balancing individual saliency with added coverage, improving results over prior methods on evaluated vision-language benchmarks.

paragraphs: SEMPO is a lightweight foundation model for time-series forecasting designed to reduce both model size and pretraining data requirements. The paper addresses the tension between broad forecasting capability and the substantial resources used by existing foundation models. Its design combines a different treatment of frequency information with a compact mechanism for adapting across datasets.

The energy-aware spectral decomposition module models both high-energy signals and informative low-energy signals that current methods can overlook. This aims to make better use of the available pretraining data. A mixture-of-prompts transformer then learns different temporal patterns through small dataset-specific prompts and adaptively routes time-series tokens to prompt-based experts.

Together, these components reduce the reported model and pretraining-data scale while maintaining strong generalization. Experiments on two large benchmarks covering 16 datasets show superior performance against evaluated state-of-the-art methods in both zero-shot and few-shot forecasting. The results support the combination of more complete spectral modeling and parameter-efficient adaptation as a route to broadly useful forecasting with a smaller resource footprint.
neurips-2025-sempo-lightweight-foundatio.tldr: SEMPO combines energy-aware spectral modeling and prompt-based experts to deliver strong forecasting with smaller models and less pretraining data.

paragraphs: FAEclust groups multidimensional functional data: observations represented by several related functions rather than a single fixed vector. The framework uses a functional autoencoder to learn a compact representation and reconstruct the original functions. Its encoder is designed to capture complex nonlinear relationships between component functions, while its decoder supports both Euclidean-valued and manifold-valued data.

The training objective includes a clustering loss, so learning the representation directly supports forming useful groups. A shape-informed objective makes those groups resistant to phase variations in the functions. This matters when changes in the alignment of a functional pattern should not dominate the grouping. Regularization of functional weights and biases further supports stability and robustness.

The authors establish a universal approximation property for the nonlinear decoder and evaluate the model through extensive experiments. The theoretical result concerns the decoder's representational capacity, while the experiments support the overall framework's effectiveness. The contribution brings nonlinear reconstruction, cluster-oriented representation learning, and resistance to phase variation into one functional-data approach.
neurips-2025-shape-informed-clustering-o.tldr: FAEclust learns functional-data representations for clustering, emphasizing shape and reducing sensitivity to phase variations.

paragraphs: STAR-Bets constructs confidence intervals for the mean of a bounded random variable, with particular attention to a fixed sampling horizon. Narrow intervals are valuable when collecting observations is expensive. The paper identifies a gap in betting-based approaches: despite strong results for confidence sequences, fixed-horizon methods have been suboptimal or empirically successful without the desired finite-time guarantee.

The proposed algorithm recalculates its betting strategy at every step, choosing a strategy that is optimal in the particular sense used by the analysis. Standard betting approaches instead choose a constant strategy in advance. The authors use this stepwise adaptation to obtain tighter guarantees, including strict improvements to classical concentration inequalities such as Hoeffding's and Bernstein's.

The paper also proves that its interval width is optimal up to a multiplicative factor of 1+o(1), which approaches one as the sample count grows. Empirical comparisons show narrower intervals than competing methods. Together, the analysis and experiments support adaptive betting as a way to improve fixed-horizon uncertainty estimates while providing theoretical guarantees for their width.
neurips-2025-star-bets-sequential-target.tldr: STAR-Bets adapts its betting strategy at each step to produce tighter fixed-horizon confidence intervals with asymptotically optimal width.

paragraphs: This paper examines how the choice of optimizer influences the kinds of solutions a neural network learns. Gradient-based training can favor simple patterns even when richer patterns would generalize better. The authors investigate this simplicity bias and find that Adam is more resistant to it than gradient descent in their theoretical setting.

They analyze two-layer ReLU networks performing binary classification on Gaussian data. Gradient descent learns a linear decision boundary with a suboptimal margin, whereas Adam develops richer, more diverse features and a nonlinear boundary closer to the Bayes-optimal predictor. An analysis of population gradients proves these results, including Adam's higher test accuracy within the distribution and under certain distribution shifts.

The authors then present experiments on datasets with spurious correlations, where SGD-trained networks are known to rely on simple patterns that can fail under shifts. The empirical results support improved generalization from Adam's richer representations in those settings. The paper connects optimizer behavior to feature learning and robustness, with its conclusions tied to the analyzed task and evaluated forms of distribution shift.
neurips-2025-the-rich-and-the-simple-on-.tldr: Theory and experiments show Adam resisting simplicity bias and learning richer features that improve generalization in the studied settings.

paragraphs: This paper tackles a chip-routing problem: connecting a collection of pins with horizontal and vertical edges while minimizing total wire length. Adding obstacles makes the task harder because routes must also avoid blocked regions. The authors identify excessive search and reliance on heuristic combinations as obstacles to effective and efficient learning-based solutions.

Their framework, OAREST, uses reinforcement learning to construct an obstacle-avoiding Rectilinear Edge Sequence tree. They first establish the optimality of this representation in obstacle-avoiding settings, providing a theoretical foundation for the construction method. A dynamic masking strategy then supports parallel training with different numbers of pins and extends to handling obstacles at inference time.

The central practical result is that the model can handle obstacles without being trained on them. Evaluations on synthetic and real-world benchmarks report superior effectiveness and efficiency for both the ordinary and obstacle-avoiding problems. The work links a theoretically supported tree representation with a training procedure that transfers to the additional routing constraints introduced at test time.
neurips-2025-train-on-pins-and-test-on-o.tldr: OAREST combines a theoretically supported routing representation with reinforcement learning to handle obstacles at inference without obstacle-based training.
